collection.description: A villager who once made a leaf whistle that scared the birds tries again for a child: a small wet noise.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: As a child, (subject) could make a leaf whistle so loud it scared the birds out of the trees. Everybody knew it. Today (child), a child, asks (subject.him/her) if (subject.he/she) can whistle with a leaf, and (subject) says, confidently, "Of course." (subject.He/She) picks a leaf, holds it between (subject.his/her) thumbs, takes a deep breath, and produces a small wet noise.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) tries again. And again. (child) sits down to watch. On the twentieth try something clicks, and the leaf lets out a shriek so loud that a flock of birds bursts out of the trees. (child) cheers. (subject) holds the leaf up like a trophy and refuses to try again, in case it doesn't work.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: "I used to be able to," (subject) admits. "I think my thumbs forgot." (child) takes a leaf, holds it the wrong way round, and immediately makes a perfect whistle. (subject) stares. "Show me how you held that," (subject.he/she) says, and the lesson goes the other way.
